newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sees relations with Kiev as top priority.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sees relations with Kiev as top priority.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin's trip to Ukraine on Friday would be his most testing and crucial foreign policy step this year, the Kremlin said.
"(It is) the most difficult visit and the most important foreign policy act by the Russian President in 1997," Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying.

Yastrzhembsky said that Yeltsin saw his trip to Kiev as even more important than a Russia-NATO summit in Paris this week at which the former Cold War foes signed a deal outlining a new cooperative relationship.
"The closer the ties between Russia and Ukraine, the fewer the headaches in its (Russia's) relations with NATO," Interfax quoted the Kremlin spokesman as saying.
Yeltsin is due to arrive in Kiev on Friday afternoon on a visit postponed over and over again due to tensions between Russia and its southern neighbour.

On Saturday, he is expected to sign a long-awaited friendship and cooperation treaty with Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, held up by a row over the division of the ex-Soviet Black Sea Fleet and its future base.

"The documents which are expected to be signed in Kiev, will become a true breakthrough in Russia's bilateral relations with Ukraine. On their basis one can resolve practically all negative problems which have appeared in recent years in relations between the two countries," Yastrzhembsky said.

Yastrzhembsky said that four documents would be signed in Kiev. Apart from the treaty, there would be a Russian-Ukrainian declaration and a joint statement on the fleet and the Black Sea port of Sevastopol where it is based.
The statement will follow on from a package of documents on the fleet signed by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his Ukrainian counterpart Pavlo Lazarenko in Kiev earlier this week.
Yastrzhembsky said the status of Sevastopol, which Ukraine agreed to lease to Russia during Chernomyrdin's visit, would not come up during Yeltsin's visit.
The Kremlin spokesman said the Sevastopol issue was used by forces in Ukraine, Russia, other former Soviet republics and abroad to try to upset relations between Moscow and Kiev.
The fourth document would be a joint statement on cooperation in the field of aerospace.
